title: C25: Stoch RSI cross vs plain RSI as a trigger (15m, 1h, 4h, 1d)

what.name: Stoch RSI
what.value_plain: 14, 14, 3, 3 (TradingView defaults); K crosses D under 20 = long, over 80 = short
what.label: SOURCED

what.name: Plain RSI
what.value_plain: RSI 14 back over 30 = long, back under 70 = short
what.label: SOURCED

what.name: Edge
what.value_plain: signal mean minus holding the same side for the same time at every bar
what.label: OURS

what.name: Costs
what.value_plain: 0.10% per round trip (Binance taker x2, backtest/fees.py); slippage and funding not modelled
what.label: SOURCED

how: stochrsi_vs_rsi.py on Binance spot from 2022; one signal per two holds.
window: 2022-01-01 to 2026-10-31, split 2022-01..2024-06 vs 2024-07..now (whole history was read: a seen-period check, not a sealed test)

verdict.label: NO intraday: no edge on 15m, 1h or 4h in either period; one small daily lead (n 17/16).

why: Stoch RSI fires about 3.5x as often as plain RSI and adds no information over it.
Daily trend-long +0.68% / +0.84% over 5 days is 1 of 32 cells with 16-17 trades: could be luck, needs its own pre-registration.
Keep it as a chart read (stretched / not stretched), not a trigger.
